architecture.title: Jev decides, your LLM writes, Jev checks — code owns every rule
architecture.caption: Jev makes the fast typed decisions (route, then verify the draft). Code keeps exact facts (language, room number), picks the approved prompt and applies the review policy. The LLM you choose in the runner's LLM picker only writes prose. Keys are read server-side (env → week24/.env.local → repo .env) and never reach the browser.

nodes.label: LLM of your choice
nodes.sub: Claude · ChatGPT · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · OpenRouter · Ollama

sequence.title: Lab 11-4 — a planted bad draft gets caught
sequence.caption: Measured live: Jev routed in ~0.5 s, Claude drafted in ~2.3 s, Jev checked each draft in ~0.4 s. The planted draft (refund + invented technician + no room number) scored 0.98 / 0.98 and was sent to human review with three reasons.

steps.label: check draft A · check planted draft B
A → staff approval · B → human review (3 reasons)
room-number rule is a plain string check — no model

charts.title: Same reply, eight providers — latency (English guest)
charts.caption: Single live observations from labs/lab03_compare_models.py (2026-09-27), parallel calls from this Mac — not a benchmark. Jev's routing decision for the same message took 520 ms. Kimi varied 12–23 s across runs; Ollama ran on a laptop GPU at $0.

charts.title: Output tokens for one ~2-sentence reply
charts.caption: Same prompt, same facts (labs/lab03_compare_models.py). Reasoning models count hidden 'thinking' as output tokens, so a 225-character reply can cost 583 tokens. Compare cost with each provider's own pricing page.
